show_hn.story_text: I want to show you HippoMaps. It is a fully featured map and navigation app built on OpenStreetMap with a custom Overpass API engine for really fast search of POIs, areas and ways. My aim with HippoMaps is to get to a level where I don't need Google Maps anymore. The biggest hurdle IMHO with OSM based apps is the lack of nice and fast search (where GMaps excels at). To get there I started working on a deterministic (as in no LLMs used) parser of queries that translates them to the Overpass QL. Search queries are split into tokens and the algorithm tries to guess "what" you want to search and "where". show_hn.title: Show HN: Foolscap – a writing app that reads your book and never writes for you
show_hn.story_text: People are scared of their ability to write and think atrophying, so I wondered: what if I built something that enhanced human creativity instead of destroying it by doing the thinking and writing for people? Foolscap is the result, or at least the first version of that idea that's fleshed out enough to share here. It reads as you write and picks out the structure: characters, ideas, threads, what's left hanging. You can respond to what it picks out, so there's a dialectic between the system and you as the writer. There's also an agent on the side, plugged into the same system, so you can ask about your book and fire off actions through conversation. It never writes into your work. show_hn.title: Show HN: erXos – a microkernel OS in Erlang based on Genera/Plan 9/QNX ideas
show_hn.story_text: What if every Erlang process were an operating-system process? With as much system code and drivers written in Erlang itself. This is something I was pondering for a while, and finally was able to prototype thanks to AI coding agents. erXos is a capability-based microkernel OS in Erlang: drivers, filesystems, and the network stack are all supervised Erlang processes, same as any app. The kernel itself is Fiasco, in C++, slightly modified for erXos needs. This is an OS I wanted for a long time: an Erlang machine where every BEAM process is a process visible to the OS and scheduler, not something bolted on top. You can try it right now with nothing to install: there is an emulator on the website that boots the whole OS in the browser ARM64 emulator. At the rc prompt, try `ps`, `top`, `ping`
